newsitem.title: USA: CNN heads meet with Cuban exiles on bureau - report.
newsitem.headline: CNN heads meet with Cuban exiles on bureau - report.

text.p: Executives from Turner Broadcasting System's Cable News Network were in Miami to meet with leaders of the Cuban exile community about opening a news bureau in Cuba, the Miami Herald reported on Saturday.

The newspaper said CNN President and Chief Executive Tom Johnson, CNN International Executive Vice President Eason Jordan, news anchor Bernard Shaw and Larry Register, the network official in charge of negotiating arrangements for the bureau with U.S. and Cuban governments, made the trip.

The four met privately with U.S. Reps. Ileana Ros-Lehtinen and Lincoln Diaz-Balart, both Miami Republicans, and with Francisco Hernandez, president of the Cuban American National Foundation, the powerful Cuban-American lobbying organization.
Officials from the various organizations were not available on Saturday to discuss the meeting.
Ros-Lehtinen said she and Diaz-Balart had criticized CNN's past coverage of Cuba for being "liberally partial to (Cuban President) Fidel Castro," the Herald said.
Executives of the Miami Herald and El Nuevo Herald, its Spanish-language affiliate, also met with the CNN executives.
Johnson defended CNN. "Our coverage has been fair and balanced," he told the newspaper.

U.S. government officials were considering whether to issue a license that would allow CNN to open a bureau in Havana. The Cuban government cleared the network to open an office, which would pave the way for CNN to become the first U.S. news agency since 1969 to station reporters and editors on the island, if Washington approves the action.
The United States has postponed a decision, expressing concern that Cuba's government might start to "pick and choose" representatives from other U.S. media.
